findings.title: decideFloor can render "at undefined" if a future caller omits level
findings.action: no action — accepted per the spec's own explicit design decision (no new fallback branch; resolveGateLevel and computeIntegrityFloor already guarantee a valid level at both reachable production entry points)
findings.disposition_rationale: The spec's HOW section explicitly lists adding a `|| "L3"` or placeholder fallback at the message site as an anti-pattern ("the branch would be unreachable dead code"), and its rationale section already names the exact boundary ("revisit if a future caller bypasses resolveGateLevel") as the accepted trade-off. Adding a fallback here would contradict the spec being built.

findings.finding_id: test/merge-gate-controlflow.test.mjs::new l3 controlflow test's two inputs (anchor level, declared-unattended config) weren't individually attributed
findings.title: new L3 controlflow test's two inputs (anchor level, declared-unattended config) weren't individually attributed
findings.action: clarified the test's comment to state which input drives refusal-firing vs. which drives the named level, verified by temporarily removing the config write and observing the leg no longer fires
findings.disposition_rationale: Verified empirically: removing the .faffrc.yaml write makes the test fail (exit 0 merge-ok, not 1 refuse) because resolveIntegrity's unattended stays false at L3 without the declared-unattended config, so unasserted-refuse never fires. The original test was correct, just under-explained. Rewrote the comment; restored the write; reran — 55/55 still pass. Committed as 29380471.
